Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of algebraic stacks.
Assume
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is quasi-compact, and
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0003> satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion.
<STRUCT_0004>
Then <MATH_0004> is universally closed.

By Lemmas <REF_0001>
and <REF_0002>
properties (1) and (2) are preserved under
any base change. By Lemma <REF_0003>
we only have to show that <MATH_0001>
is closed, whenever <MATH_0002> is an affine scheme mapping into <MATH_0003>.
Hence it suffices to show: if <MATH_0004> is a
quasi-compact morphism from an algebraic stack to an affine scheme
satisfying the existence part of the valuative criterion,
then <MATH_0005> is closed. Let <MATH_0006> be a closed subset.
We have to show that <MATH_0007> is closed to finish the proof.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Let <MATH_0008> be the reduced induced
algebraic stack structure on <MATH_0009> (Properties of Stacks,
Definition <REF_0004>).
Then <MATH_0010> is a closed immersion
and we have to show that the image of <MATH_0011>
is closed. Since closed immersions are quasi-compact
(Lemma <REF_0005>)
and satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion
(Lemma <REF_0006>)
and since compositions of quasi-compact morphisms are quasi-compact
(Lemma <REF_0007>)
and since compositions preserve the property of satisfying
the existence part of the valuative criterion
(Lemma <REF_0008>)
we conclude that it suffices to show: if <MATH_0012>
is a quasi-compact morphism from an algebraic stack to an affine scheme
satisfying the existence part of the valuative criterion,
then <MATH_0013> is closed.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Since <MATH_0014> is quasi-compact (being quasi-compact over the
affine <MATH_0015>), we can choose an affine scheme <MATH_0016> and a surjective
smooth morphism <MATH_0017>
(Properties of Stacks, Lemma
<REF_0009>).
Suppose that <MATH_0018> is in the closure of the image of <MATH_0019>
(in other words, in the closure of the image of <MATH_0020>).
Then by
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0010>
we can find a valuation ring <MATH_0021> with fraction field <MATH_0022>
and a commutative diagram
<MATH_0023>
such that the closed point of <MATH_0024> maps to <MATH_0025>. By assumption
we get an extension <MATH_0026> and a valuation ring <MATH_0027>
dominating <MATH_0028> and the dotted arrow in the following diagram
<MATH_0029>
Thus <MATH_0030> is in the image of <MATH_0031> and we win.
